Dear Dr. Vance,

Thank you for agreeing to assess Lucas, a three-month-old boy who has been admitted under our care following findings initially detected on antenatal sonography. He lives at home with both parents, and the family history is unremarkable.

Cardiovascular evaluation confirmed a solitary common great vessel issuing from the ventricular base directly above a prominent communication within the interventricular septum. The systemic arch continues normally to the left, with no arch interruption or right-sided branching. We found no evidence of classic Fallot-type morphology, the tricuspid valve orifice is patent, and there is no pulmonary outflow narrowing. Furthermore, all pulmonary veins insert normally into the left atrium, excluding anomalous venous drainage. 

Over the past three days, Lucas has developed oliguria, and bloodwork indicates compromised kidney function, marked by a progressive rise in serum creatinine levels. A renal sonogram revealed two distinct, non-fused renal units without lower pole bridging or internal cystic lesions. 

His head circumference is tracking along the 45th percentile, displaying normal cranial growth, and neuroimaging previously demonstrated a fully developed, intact corpus callosum. Enteral feeding has been tolerated without chronic diarrhea, edema, or enteric protein loss. A three-vessel cord was documented at delivery with two umbilical arteries present. He is presently taking oral vitamin D and low-dose furosemide. 

I would welcome your expert assessment regarding his systemic and cardiovascular presentation and your guidance on ongoing care.

Warm regards,

Dr. Arthur Pendelton
